independence: The design witness was written and saved from the actual Old English before the source editor's translation was opened. The main independent learner solver has not participated in these audits and must not see either witness before freezing solutions.
agreements: Both preserve all clauses in the exact 236-word music-and-summons span and stop at mid wes.
Owini performs the outdoor work, hears and follows the music with his attention, considers its significance, and enters at the signal. Chad opens the window, signals and speaks the summons.
The fronted accusatives stefne and sang depend on embedded gehīerde, as original note 8 states. Plural nēalǣcton continues voice and song; the later masculine hē denotes the song.
The oratory and the communal church are distinct. The seven brothers are summoned, and Owini is explicitly included as well.
The half-hour interval, return along the previous route, interpretive force of hwæt ðā ðing bēon sceolden and purpose of the signal agree.

accepted_rendering_differences.decision: Both express the past background. Neither changes the companions into the subject of Owini's hearing.

accepted_rendering_differences.anchor: eall gefylde and in ymbhwyrfte ymbsealde
alternatives: filled everything and surrounded it all around
filled the whole place and surrounded it on every side
accepted_rendering_differences.decision: Both render the surrounding extent without introducing a human actor. Whole place is an explicit English contextual expansion of eall, which original note 12 identifies as accusative singular; it is not an extra Old English noun.

accepted_rendering_differences.anchor: and ðū ēac swilce mid wes
alternatives: and you too be with them
and be present with them yourself as well
accepted_rendering_differences.decision: Both preserve the explicit inclusion of Owini. The local help supplies the accompanying/present force of adverbial mid with the command wes.
